title: Vectors, lines and planes
summary: Vector algebra, scalar and vector products, vector equations of lines and planes, and the angles and intersections between them.

keyterms.definition: The length of a vector: |v| = √(v₁² + v₂² + v₃²).
A vector of magnitude 1; v/|v| points in the direction of v.
The vector from the origin O to a point.
v · w = v₁w₁ + v₂w₂ + v₃w₃ = |v||w| cos θ; zero for perpendicular vectors.
v × w, a vector perpendicular to both v and w with magnitude |v||w| sin θ.
r = a + λb, where a is a point on the line and b a direction vector.
Lines in 3D that are neither parallel nor intersecting.
A vector perpendicular to a plane.
r · n = a · n, or ax + by + cz = d where (a, b, c) is a normal.
|v × w| is the area of the parallelogram with sides v and w; half of it gives a triangle.

questions.explanation: 4 − 2 + 6 = 8. A scalar product is a number, not a vector.

questions.text: Two non-zero vectors are perpendicular exactly when their scalar product is ___.

questions.statement: The line r = (1, 0, 2) + λ(3, −1, 4) passes through (4, −1, 6).

questions.prompt: Find the unit vector in the direction of (3, 0, 4).
questions.explanation: The magnitude is 5; divide each component by 5.

questions.text: Two lines in 3D that are not parallel and do not intersect are called ___.
questions.explanation: Skew lines are impossible in 2D but common in 3D.

questions.statement: v · w = |v||w| cos θ, where θ is the angle between v and w.
questions.explanation: This is how the scalar product gives angles.

questions.prompt: Match each expression to what it is.

pairs.right: A vector perpendicular to v and w
Area of the parallelogram on v and w
Unit vector in the direction of v

questions.explanation: Keep track of whether each result is a number or a vector.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to decide whether two non-parallel lines intersect.
items: Equate the x, y and z components of the two lines
Solve two of the equations for λ and μ
Substitute λ and μ into the third equation
If it holds the lines intersect; otherwise they are skew
questions.explanation: Three equations, two unknowns: the third equation is the test.

questions.prompt: Find i × j, where i = (1, 0, 0) and j = (0, 1, 0).
questions.explanation: i × j = k, following the right-hand rule.
(2 × 3 − 0 × 1, 0 × 0 − 1 × 3, 1 × 1 − 2 × 0) = (6, −3, 1). Check: it is perpendicular to both vectors.

questions.text: The plane 2x − y + 3z = 7 has normal vector (2, −1, ___).
questions.explanation: The coefficients of x, y and z form a normal.
The vector product is anti-commutative: v × w = −(w × v).

questions.prompt: Which point lies on the plane 2x − y + 3z = 7?
The angle between a line with direction d and a plane with normal n is…
options: 180° minus the angle between d and n
90° minus the angle between d and n
the angle between d and n
questions.explanation: The normal is perpendicular to the plane, so subtract from 90° (or use sin instead of cos).

questions.text: The area of a triangle with two sides given by vectors v and w is ½|v ___ w|.
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the vector product is the parallelogram area.

questions.statement: A plane can be written r = a + λb + μc, where b and c are non-parallel vectors in the plane.
questions.explanation: This is the vector (parametric) form of a plane.

questions.prompt: Match each equation to its type.

questions.explanation: You should be able to convert between these forms.
